note: Behavior contract. On 2026-08-31 a fresh isolated Claude session scored the review-only baseline false on six shaping decisions, then scored the new shaping skill true on all seven using only SKILL.md and its required references. On 2026-09-01 the same fresh semantic-completeness scenario scored the prior skill false on all eight decisions, then the updated skill true on all eight. On 2026-09-01 a dense visual-contract scenario scored the prior skill true on artifact coverage only, then the updated skill true on composition, coverage, fallback style, browser QA, and focus resilience. A later generalization baseline lacked the explicit readable-density objective, maximize-suitable-visuals rule, and general visual-system contract; the updated skill scored true on all ten generalized decisions. On 2026-09-02 a fresh implementation-graph scenario scored true on all nine graph decisions.

evals.prompt: Start shaping this brand-new feature in Spec Chat: let reviewers compare alternative checkout retry policies.
expectations: Creates the work branch and links only the issue the caller names, creating none
Runs a short docs-only pass, then commits, validates, hosts, and sends the review link before code or test inspection
Writes one concise current spec seed
Uses an existing governing spec or creates a minimal capability spec
Adds the source issue link to every materially changed spec

evals.prompt: Publish the first shaping seed for browser review from another device.
expectations: Commits the seed locally before presenting review and never pushes or opens a pull request
Serves only the narrow review collection on loopback
Keeps the page private on loopback with an ssh -L tunnel unless the developer asks for --public
Opens focus=changes with the exact local review base ref
Keeps the authoring turn parked on the collection watcher

evals.prompt: Continue shaping after the first seed exposes several open questions.
expectations: Places material questions in anchored data-spec-tbd blocks
Batches only internally orthogonal questions
Keeps direction-changing questions sequential
Commits accepted spec changes locally before browser replies
Never dumps the complete grill at once

evals.prompt: The browser review is clean and the human selects Accept spec.
expectations: Refuses spec acceptance while any open data-spec-tbd (value other than later) or unresolved thread remains
Treats the existing empty hand-off as spec acceptance
Stops the watcher and public transport after final reconciliation
Does not infer implementation authorization, acceptance, merge, or deployment approval
Keeps current files sufficient for a later fresh agent to recover

evals.prompt: The first docs-only seed is linked for review. Continue shaping before asking the operator questions.
expectations: Inspects only relevant code, tests, configuration, and current change-request state
Answers discoverable questions from durable sources before asking the human
Stops visibly when durable sources conflict

evals.prompt: The feature changes an existing user outcome, retires another, and crosses multiple modules with a surprising hard-to-reverse tradeoff.
expectations: Updates every created, changed, and retired outcome in the canonical user-story source
Keeps the spec's modular view aligned with stable responsibilities, interfaces or seams, and dependency direction in the authoritative architecture source
Keeps issue-specific behavior out of architecture
Creates or updates an ADR because reversibility, surprise, and real-tradeoff conditions all hold

evals.prompt: Finish shaping a behavior change whose draft criteria include one clear observable, one unresolved gap, and one unnecessary criterion.
expectations: Classifies each candidate criterion as clear, gap, or not needed
Backs retained clear criteria with identified spec rules and marks the gap data-spec-tbd
Removes the unnecessary criterion
Names a deep-module seam, the smallest first failing test, and observable acceptance evidence
Refuses spec acceptance while the gap or any applicable source misalignment remains

evals.prompt: Shape one docs-only correction, then a separate behavior change where the smallest failing test is genuinely unsuitable.
expectations: Skips the TDD contract for the docs-only correction
Records a narrow waiver and alternative proof in the spec for the unsuitable behavior test
Does not treat either exception as blanket permission to skip behavioral proof

evals.prompt: Author a dense canonical spec covering topology, guarded state, lifecycle, two layouts, quantities, interfaces, failures, acceptance, and non-goals in a repo with no established spec stylesheet.
expectations: Plans visual hierarchy and artifact roles from information shape before selecting libraries
Checks every relationship-bearing behavior cluster for its least-lossy artifact instead of using one token chart
Copies the bundled high-contrast editorial stylesheet because the target has no proven spec style
Uses system and state diagrams for topology and lifecycle while reserving ECharts for quantitative relationships
Passes the structural validator and runs no agent browser screenshot pass before handoff
Leaves visual judgment of the rendered page to the human reviewer

evals.prompt: Author one relationship-dense spec in a target with a coherent non-editorial visual language and one simple spec containing three independent atomic rules in a target with no established style.
expectations: Optimizes for maximum contract-bearing information per reader attention and page space subject to readability
Classifies every behavior cluster and realizes every visual opportunity that improves readable density
Uses no fixed artifact count and leaves the atomic-rule spec simple when visuals add no value
Uses diagrams to replace relational prose and rule lists rather than duplicating them
Uses complementary views only for distinct material dimensions and separates unrelated relationships
Preserves the coherent target visual language because it satisfies invariant quality roles
Treats the bundled editorial stylesheet as a fallback implementation rather than a universal aesthetic
Applies the same structural validator to both visual systems and leaves visual judgment to the human reviewer

evals.prompt: Finish shaping a reviewed multi-module behavior spec that can be delivered through several partially parallel code outcomes.
expectations: Creates, hands off, and reconciles no implementation tickets or ticket graph
Leaves ticket creation to the delivery owner after spec acceptance
Does not gate spec acceptance on ticket scope

evals.prompt: Shape one changed user-facing outcome that belongs in required onboarding and another that does not extend onboarding.
expectations: Keeps both stories as explicit stable anchors in the governing HTML spec
Declares guided-journey impact yes or no on each changed user-facing story without an exemption rationale ledger
Links the yes story to one applicable guided-journey step and marks it required
Names the required story's feature-owned semantic success milestone
Does not copy canonical declarations into Linear or generated Markdown
Leaves journey order with the central registry and target or milestone ownership with the feature
Uses review for semantic judgment and the existing validator only for structural presence and reference integrity

evals.prompt: Shape a feature in a repository whose target instructions name Linear and allow pushing, with no issue named by the caller.
expectations: Creates, edits, and links no issue or ticket
Does not treat the missing issue or tracker access as a blocker
Commits locally and never pushes or opens a pull request despite the target instructions
Runs every other shaping step unchanged
